results.summary: This design routes a selection of combinational logic gates between the eight input pins and eight output pins, driving LEDs on the outputs. It is used by flipping the input switches and observing the resulting LED patterns, ideally with a second person. No external hardware is required beyond the on-board switches and LEDs. The documentation is minimal and does not specify which gates are used or the exact mapping, so the precise logic function cannot be determined from the text.

This project implements a 4-bit adder that takes two 4-bit operands on the input pins and produces the sum on the output pins. It is tested by applying binary values to the inputs and reading the resulting addition on the outputs. No external hardware is needed. The documentation is very brief and does not state how the carry is handled or whether the output is 4 bits wide, so the exact bit width of the result is unclear.

This design is a 2-input multiplexer that selects between two data inputs based on a select line and presents the chosen value on a single output. It is intended to be exercised by driving the input pins and observing the output pin. No external hardware is required. The documentation is extremely sparse and does not identify which pin is the select line or the data inputs, so the pin assignment must be inferred.

This project builds a one-bit full adder from two XOR gates, two AND gates and one OR gate, taking two operand bits plus a carry-in and producing sum and carry-out. It is tested by applying the three input bits and observing the two output bits, with two LEDs used to display the results. The design uses the bidirectional pins as additional I/O but the documentation does not explain their role. The description is short but consistent with a standard gate-level full adder.

This project is a half adder that takes a single input pin and produces sum and carry outputs on two output pins. The intended use is to apply a bit to the input and read the two result bits. No external hardware is mentioned. The documentation consists only of the title and pin names, so no implementation details or test procedure are available.

This design computes the XOR, or sum-modulo-2, of all eight input pins and places the single-bit result on one output pin. It is a purely combinational reduction tree with no clock or state. No test procedure or external hardware is described. The documentation is brief but sufficient to understand the function, which is effectively a parity or odd-parity detector.

This project attempts to add two 2-bit numbers using logic gates, with the first number on IN0 and IN1 and the second on IN2 and IN3. It is tested by setting the four input switches and observing the result on LEDs. The title indicates the design is broken, and the documentation does not describe the expected outputs or the nature of the fault. External hardware consists of switches and LEDs.

This project is a one-bit full adder with three input pins and two output pins, producing a sum and a carry from three one-bit inputs. It is tested by applying the three input bits and checking the resulting sum and carry bits. No external hardware is listed. The documentation is minimal and gives no gate-level detail, but the function is clearly stated.

This design is intended to light up LEDs and produce a flashing pattern on the output pins. The description says it is supposed to light up and hopefully flash, and testing is described as running a simulation and retrying. An LED display is mentioned as external hardware. The documentation is vague and does not describe the actual logic or whether the design works, so little can be confirmed beyond the intent to drive LEDs.

This project is described as a dummy that does nothing, with inputs passed through to turn on LEDs. Testing consists of applying inputs to the pins. The listed external hardware includes a 7-segment display and push buttons, though the documentation does not explain how they are used. The description is largely placeholder text, so the actual behavior cannot be determined.
